Introduction

•   In earlier robot control models, each joint was often treated as an independent,
    linear constant-coefficient 2nd Order differential equation.

   – coupling between joints varies with motion,
   – damping and dynamic effects are not uniform across
      the workspace.

citations.evidenceText:
Nonlinear Time-Varying Approach

•  For nonlinear control, one important idea is to use a control input that cancels
   nonlinear effects, so the closed-loop system behaves in a simpler way.
•  Hence it is called a linearizing control law.
•  Fixed gains cannot keep the system at one desired pole location, such as critical
   damping.
•  A better approach is to use time-varying gains that change with the system
    state. This keeps the overall stiffness or response behavior approximately
   constant.
•   In a partitioned control law, the standard servo part
   remains unchanged, while the model-based part
   handles the nonlinear dynamics.

•  Time-Varying Nature of Manipulator Systems
•  Payload Changes
   – Picking up or releasing objects changes 𝑀Θ  dynamically. A fixed controller

       wear. Calibration becomes outdated.

   – Motor heating changes winding resistance, affecting
      torque output.

   – Human-robot collaboration introduces unknown, time-

citations.evidenceText:
Multi-input, Multi-output control systems
  •  Control law structure:
                  𝑭= 𝜶𝑭′ + 𝜷
  •  where:
 𝑭→ 𝑛× 1 vector of actuator inputs                𝑭′ →𝑛× 1 vector of servo
 commands
 𝜶→ 𝑛× 𝑛 matrix                  𝜷→ 𝑛× 1 vector
• 𝜶 is not necessarily diagonal
•   It is chosen to decouple the coupled equations of motion
•    If 𝜶 and 𝜷 are chosen correctly:
   – each joint behaves like an independent unit mass
   – the nonlinear system becomes easier to control
   – Hence, it’s called Linearizing and Decoupling Control Law.

concepts.title: Distinguish effective inertia from body mass
concepts.description: Joint-space inertia depends on geometry and mass distribution relative to moving joint axes, not only on each link’s fixed mass.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish effective inertia from body mass

concepts.title: Identify the velocity-dependent dynamics term
concepts.description: V contains the stated velocity-dependent coupling; G is gravity and M multiplies the actual generalized acceleration.
concepts.subtopic: Identify the velocity-dependent dynamics term

concepts.title: Use the rigid manipulator mass-matrix property
concepts.description: The quadratic kinetic-energy form uses a symmetric positive-definite inertia matrix; coupling generally permits off-diagonal elements.
concepts.subtopic: Use the rigid manipulator mass-matrix property

concepts.title: Separate actuator input from external torque
concepts.description: With the declared assisting-positive contact convention, both actuator and external torques enter the right side; their meanings must not be conflated.
concepts.subtopic: Separate actuator input from external torque

concepts.title: Trace a payload change beyond a disturbance term
concepts.description: A carried payload changes the moving mass distribution and gravitational load; it is not generally captured by a single constant external torque.
concepts.subtopic: Trace a payload change beyond a disturbance term

concepts.title: Qualify the fixed-controller failure claim
concepts.description: Model mismatch can degrade control, but a robust controller or a small admissible payload may still meet requirements.
concepts.subtopic: Qualify the fixed-controller failure claim

concepts.title: Separate winding resistance from regulated torque
concepts.description: For the same current and torque constant, electromagnetic torque is unchanged; the resistive voltage drop increases.
concepts.subtopic: Separate winding resistance from regulated torque

concepts.title: Interpret the configuration photographs
concepts.description: The photographs show geometry changes, but do not supply the quantitative data needed to calculate or rank every joint inertia.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret the configuration photographs

concepts.title: Interpret a moving operating-point model
concepts.description: The Jacobians are evaluated at a trajectory-dependent operating point, so the local linear coefficients can vary in time even when the original model is autonomous.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret a moving operating-point model

concepts.title: Choose when to reconsider a local linear model
concepts.description: A local approximation must be checked over the intended operating range; neither exact global validity nor a universal ban on linear methods follows.
concepts.subtopic: Choose when to reconsider a local linear model

concepts.title: Distinguish physical and normalized gains
concepts.description: The state-dependent model part and fixed normalized servo part have different roles.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish physical and normalized gains

concepts.title: Identify a condition needed for exact cancellation
concepts.description: Exact algebra assumes the demanded input reaches the plant; saturation leaves a residual not removed by the derivation.
concepts.subtopic: Identify a condition needed for exact cancellation

concepts.title: Distinguish a cubic spring coefficient from stiffness
concepts.description: Force requires q to have units N/m³; differentiating qx³ gives the tangent stiffness 3qx², while qx² is the secant ratio for nonzero x.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish a cubic spring coefficient from stiffness

concepts.title: Evaluate the cubic spring scaling
concepts.description: The cubic force scales as x³ while its derivative scales as x².
concepts.subtopic: Evaluate the cubic spring scaling

concepts.title: Read the cubic restoring-force graph
concepts.description: Cubing a negative displacement preserves its negative sign and f_s(-x)=-f_s(x).
concepts.subtopic: Read the cubic restoring-force graph

concepts.title: Interpret signs in the cubic spring plant
concepts.description: Moving the resisting terms to the right gives m ẍ=f−b ẋ−q x³.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret signs in the cubic spring plant

concepts.title: Convert physical closed-loop stiffness to normalized gains
concepts.description: Dividing the desired physical error equation by m gives k_p=k_CL/m=9; critical damping requires k_v=2√k_p=6.
concepts.subtopic: Convert physical closed-loop stiffness to normalized gains

concepts.title: Interpret the normalized servo signal
concepts.description: The product m f′ must have force units, so f′ is an acceleration command.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret the normalized servo signal

concepts.title: Derive the normalized cubic plant
concepts.description: The same viscous and cubic terms cancel from both sides, leaving m ẍ=m f′ and then ẍ=f′.
concepts.subtopic: Derive the normalized cubic plant

concepts.title: Calculate a compensated force
concepts.description: The inertia term is 6 N, the viscous term is −1 N and the cubic term is 0.5 N, giving 5.5 N.
concepts.subtopic: Calculate a compensated force

concepts.title: Derive the homogeneous tracking-error equation
concepts.description: Differentiate the declared error twice: ë=ẍ_d−ẍ=−k_v ė−k_p e.
concepts.subtopic: Derive the homogeneous tracking-error equation

concepts.title: Trace measured signals in the partitioned-control diagram
concepts.description: The plant’s actual b ẋ+q x³ terms are canceled using measured actual state, while desired quantities enter the servo calculation.
concepts.subtopic: Trace measured signals in the partitioned-control diagram

concepts.title: Distinguish viscous and Coulomb friction at nonzero speed
concepts.description: Viscous resistance is proportional to velocity, while the ideal Coulomb term changes sign but has fixed nonzero-speed magnitude.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish viscous and Coulomb friction at nonzero speed

concepts.title: Separate the printed sign law from static friction
concepts.description: The numerical sign function uses zero at zero; a static-friction interval is a different model and the plotted endpoints do not define two simultaneous scalar outputs.
concepts.subtopic: Separate the printed sign law from static friction

concepts.title: Determine the physical friction direction
concepts.description: The physical force is −b_c sgn(ẋ); negative velocity gives a positive resisting force.
concepts.subtopic: Determine the physical friction direction

concepts.title: Identify the terms in the second spring example
concepts.description: The second example uses Coulomb friction and a linear spring; it does not silently retain the earlier viscous/cubic terms.
concepts.subtopic: Identify the terms in the second spring example

concepts.title: Select the compensating term for the Coulomb plant
concepts.description: The positive compensation reproduces the actual LHS resisting terms so they cancel after substitution.
concepts.subtopic: Select the compensating term for the Coulomb plant

concepts.title: Compute the Coulomb and spring compensation
concepts.description: The inertia term is 6 N, Coulomb compensation is −0.4 N and spring compensation is 0.5 N, so the sum is 6.1 N.
concepts.subtopic: Compute the Coulomb and spring compensation

concepts.title: Derive the residual from an underestimated Coulomb coefficient
concepts.description: Actual acceleration equals f′+(b̂_c−b_c)sgn(ẋ)/m; subtracting it from desired acceleration reverses that residual sign in the error equation.
concepts.subtopic: Derive the residual from an underestimated Coulomb coefficient

concepts.title: Find critical damping of the normalized error equation
concepts.description: The characteristic polynomial s²+8s+16=(s+4)² has a repeated negative root.
concepts.subtopic: Find critical damping of the normalized error equation

concepts.title: Use the pendulum angle convention
concepts.description: Gravity produces physical clockwise torque −mgl cosθ, so moving it to the left gives +mgl cosθ.
concepts.subtopic: Use the pendulum angle convention

concepts.title: Separate nonlinear dynamics from varying inertia
concepts.description: A nonlinear second-order model can have constant inertia; cosθ and sign-dependent friction already introduce nonlinearity.
concepts.subtopic: Separate nonlinear dynamics from varying inertia

concepts.title: Calculate gravity holding torque at two poses
concepts.description: The holding input is mgl cosθ; cosine is one at the horizontal pose and zero at the upright pose.
concepts.subtopic: Calculate gravity holding torque at two poses

concepts.title: Choose the pendulum model term
concepts.description: Exact model cancellation uses the actual measured velocity and angle in each corresponding physical term.
concepts.subtopic: Choose the pendulum model term

concepts.title: Identify desired-acceleration feedforward
concepts.description: Both the actual source equation and diagram use desired angular acceleration. It has the same units as k_v ė and k_p e when k_v is s⁻¹ and k_p is s⁻²; the earlier missing-dot claim was a visual-reading error, not a source defect.
concepts.subtopic: Resolve the missing derivative dot explicitly

concepts.title: Trace the torque partition in the block diagram
concepts.description: Despite the τ′ label, the normalized servo has angular-acceleration units; inertia multiplication produces torque before adding β.
concepts.subtopic: Trace the torque partition in the block diagram

concepts.title: Read the desired trajectory function
concepts.description: The conversion returns a constant π/2 radians; the two derivative outputs are zero.
concepts.subtopic: Read the desired trajectory function

concepts.title: Read the physical and normalized parameters
concepts.description: The code follows the inertia, friction and normalized-gain definitions of the displayed model.
concepts.subtopic: Read the physical and normalized parameters

concepts.title: Interpret the controller return tuple
concepts.description: The return statement is tau,e,e_dot,f_prime; these diagnostic values are not the plant state.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret the controller return tuple

concepts.title: Calculate the controller error signs
concepts.description: Both errors are desired minus actual: π/2−π/6=π/3 and 0−0.5=−0.5.
concepts.subtopic: Calculate the controller error signs

concepts.title: Prevent a degree-radian gravity error
concepts.description: NumPy trigonometric functions use radians, and the source explicitly converts the desired angle with deg2rad.
concepts.subtopic: Prevent a degree-radian gravity error

concepts.title: Read the ODE state and derivative order
concepts.description: The derivative of angle is angular velocity and the derivative of angular velocity is angular acceleration.
concepts.subtopic: Read the ODE state and derivative order

concepts.title: Interpret the underscore assignments
concepts.description: Tuple unpacking receives all four values; repeated underscore is a conventional name for unused values, not an operation that changes the function.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret the underscore assignments

concepts.title: Interpret the solver tolerances
concepts.description: Solver tolerances guide adaptive numerical error control; they do not validate the model, measurements, actuator limits or hardware.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret the solver tolerances

concepts.title: Identify what is missing from the displayed executable snippet
concepts.description: The screenshots show controller and plant functions but omit the import and integration setup definitions.
concepts.subtopic: Identify what is missing from the displayed executable snippet

concepts.description: Subtracting −20 from 90 gives 110 degrees, which must be converted to radians.
concepts.subtopic: Reconstruct the plotted initial tracking error

concepts.title: Reproduce the displayed initial pendulum torque
concepts.description: The normalized acceleration is16×110π/180≈30.7178; zero-speed viscous/Coulomb terms vanish, and gravity adds9.81cos(−20°)≈9.2184, giving39.9362 N·m.

concepts.title: Use the full critical-damping initial-condition solution
concepts.description: A repeated root−4 gives (A+Bt)e^(−4t); e(0)=e0 sets A=e0 and zero initial derivative sets B=4e0.
concepts.subtopic: Use the full critical-damping initial-condition solution

concepts.title: State what the matched-model simulation does not establish
concepts.description: The plots demonstrate a particular nominal simulation, not untested mismatch, saturation or hardware cases.
concepts.subtopic: State what the matched-model simulation does not establish

concepts.title: Explain the ideal Coulomb torque near the final pose
concepts.description: The ideal sign law depends on the sign of actual speed, not its small magnitude or desired speed; it is discontinuous at zero.
concepts.subtopic: Explain the ideal Coulomb torque near the final pose

concepts.title: Map the angle to the link endpoint
concepts.description: The horizontal reference gives x=lcosθ and y=lsinθ; the negative angle places the endpoint below the positive horizontal axis.
concepts.subtopic: Map the angle to the link endpoint

concepts.title: Read the phase portrait’s plotted state
concepts.description: The phase plot labels its axes θ(rad) and θ_dot(rad/s), so it traces actual angle-speed state.
concepts.subtopic: Read the phase portrait’s plotted state

concepts.title: Calculate animation endpoint velocity
concepts.description: Differentiation gives ẋ=−l sinθ·θ̇ and ẏ=l cosθ·θ̇; at upright with positive speed, the endpoint moves left.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish an animation frame from executable animation code

concepts.title: Keep vector reference derivatives consistent
concepts.description: The velocity and acceleration references must be first and second time derivatives of the desired position, not independent arbitrary signals.
concepts.subtopic: Keep vector reference derivatives consistent

concepts.title: Interpret coupling in an n-joint model
concepts.description: Off-diagonal entries represent inertial coupling between the chosen generalized coordinates.
concepts.subtopic: Interpret coupling in an n-joint model

concepts.title: Check the vector partition dimensions
concepts.description: The matrix-vector product αF′ must be an n-component column vector so it can be added to β and equal F.
concepts.subtopic: Check the vector partition dimensions

concepts.title: Derive the normalized coupled plant
concepts.description: Cancel h to obtain M Ẍ=M F′ and multiply by M⁻¹; off-diagonal coupling does not prevent exact full-matrix cancellation.

concepts.description: The matrix product is[2−2,1−6]=[0,−5]; addingβ gives[0.5,−4].

concepts.title: Distinguish diagonal servo gains from a diagonal plant
concepts.description: Diagonal normalized gains separate the ideal error equations; that is a controller/model transformation, not a claim about uncoupled physical inertia or identical gains.
concepts.subtopic: Distinguish diagonal servo gains from a diagonal plant

concepts.title: Select critical gains for two normalized joint errors
concepts.description: Apply k_v,i=2√k_p,i componentwise:2√9=6 and2√25=10.
concepts.subtopic: Select critical gains for two normalized joint errors

concepts.title: Write the vector tracking-error equation
concepts.description: Subtract the normalized actual acceleration from desired acceleration; the feedforward terms cancel, leaving negative error feedback on the right.
concepts.subtopic: Write the vector tracking-error equation
